purpose: Versioned scoring profiles for historical-language hypotheses. Scores rank candidates within one profile and compare profiles by mean log-probability per letter; they are not calibrated probabilities and never a probability that a reading is historically correct.

baseline.disclosure: The modern-English model built from Cipher Museum exhibit prose remains available and is clearly a BASELINE: modern English, museum register, not historical material.

abstention.calibratedOn: development probes recorded in this file
abstention.note: Below any threshold the comparison reports no decision. Abstention is a result, not a failure.

profiles.register: Essayistic prose: reflective, classicizing, heavy in Latin quotation.
profiles.orthography: Original early-modern spelling retained: undifferentiated i/j and u/v, -oit imperfects, s before consonants (mesme, estre).
profiles.relevance: Closest published profile to the French of the 1578–1584 Mary Stuart correspondence, but a different author, register and decade.
profiles.limits: One author, one volume. Not chancery or diplomatic French, and not a substitute for the orthography of any particular scribe.

sources.work: Michel de Montaigne, Essais, Volume I (first published 1580)
sources.edition: Project Gutenberg eBook 48529, a bilingual edition presenting the original text beside a modern-French rendering.

orthographyProbe.scope: Build check that the extraction kept original 1580s spelling, not the modern rendering printed alongside it.

profiles.normalization: Uppercase; accents and ligatures folded to A–Z (É→E, Æ→AE, ß→SS and so on); every other character removed; no n-gram crosses a source line break. Folding is lossy.
profiles.pruning: Published counts keep the 20000 most frequent quadgrams and 6000 most frequent trigrams. Anything else scores at the floor.
profiles.rights: Pre-1800 work, public domain worldwide. Only n-gram counts are published here; no part of the transcription is redistributed.

coverage.holdoutNote: The final 5% of each source was reserved before counting and is written to holdout.json. The model has not seen it, but it is the same work by the same author: a document-internal holdout, not an independent source document.
coverage.note: Token share kept is the fraction of training n-gram occurrences that a published count covers. Unseen text will fall to the floor more often than these figures suggest.

profiles.orthography: Original Tuscan spelling with elision marks; apostrophes and accents are removed by the normalization below.
profiles.relevance: An Italian profile with period orthography, for comparison against French and Latin hypotheses.
profiles.limits: Verse, not prose. Fourteenth-century Tuscan is two centuries earlier than the chancery Italian of most enciphered diplomatic correspondence; letter statistics from verse carry metrical structure that prose does not.

profiles.orthography: Classical orthography with u for consonantal v; no medieval e-caudata or ae/e confusion.
profiles.relevance: Latin appears inside French, Italian and German historical ciphers; a Latin profile lets that hypothesis be tested rather than assumed.
profiles.limits: Classical Latin, NOT the medieval or early-modern ecclesiastical and chancery Latin that actually appears in enciphered archives. Expect this profile to understate the real variation.
